name: Most frequent L1_model by strong or soft Stack status
description: Use ONLY when the question asks for strong vs soft Stack status (max non-Stack test_score vs Stack test_score) and wants the top L1_model per STATUS with OCCURRENCES. Strong: any step with max(non-Stack test) < Stack test; soft: equal; one status per name+version (strong wins). Output columns STATUS, L1_MODEL, OCCURRENCES. Do NOT use for questions that merely ask which L1_model / model category appears most frequently when comparing Traditional models to Stack (no strong/soft language), and do not use for raw L1 frequency over model or stack_ok alone.
sql: WITH non_stack AS (SELECT name, version, step, MAX(test_score) AS max_non_stack FROM model_score WHERE model <> 'Stack' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3), stack AS (SELECT name, version, step, test_score AS stack_score FROM model_score WHERE model = 'Stack'), step_status AS (SELECT s.name, s.version, s.step, m.L1_model, CASE WHEN n.max_non_stack < s.stack_score THEN 'strong' WHEN n.max_non_stack = s.stack_score THEN 'soft' END AS status FROM stack AS s JOIN non_stack AS n USING (name, version, step) JOIN model AS m USING (name, version, step)), per_model AS (SELECT name, version, L1_model, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'strong' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'strong' WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'soft' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'soft' END AS status FROM step_status WHERE status IS NOT NULL GROUP BY name, version, L1_model), counts AS (SELECT status AS STATUS, L1_model AS L1_MODEL, COUNT(*) AS OCCURRENCES FROM per_model WHERE status IS NOT NULL GROUP BY status, L1_model), ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY STATUS ORDER BY OCCURRENCES DESC, L1_MODEL) AS rn FROM counts) SELECT STATUS, L1_MODEL, OCCURRENCES FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1

name: Most frequent L1_model across Traditional model and Stack rows
description: Use when asking which L1_model / model category appears most frequently comparing Traditional models to Stack, without strong/soft status. Count L1_model rows from model as Traditional and from stack_ok as Stack; sum per L1_model; return the top L1_model with traditional_count, stack_count, and total_occurrences. Do NOT classify strong/soft from model_score test scores.
sql: WITH source_counts AS (SELECT L1_model, 'Traditional' AS model_source, COUNT(*) AS occurrence_count FROM model GROUP BY L1_model UNION ALL SELECT L1_model, 'Stack' AS model_source, COUNT(*) AS occurrence_count FROM stack_ok GROUP BY L1_model), category_totals AS (SELECT L1_model, SUM(CASE WHEN model_source = 'Traditional' THEN occurrence_count ELSE 0 END) AS traditional_count, SUM(CASE WHEN model_source = 'Stack' THEN occurrence_count ELSE 0 END) AS stack_count, SUM(occurrence_count) AS total_occurrences FROM source_counts GROUP BY L1_model), ranked AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_occurrences DESC) AS occurrence_rank FROM category_totals) SELECT L1_model, traditional_count, stack_count, total_occurrences FROM ranked WHERE occurrence_rank = 1
